key_insight: MARTINI-3 coarse-grained clay parameters accurately capture phyllosilicate polarity and show that amphiphilic clay can strongly compatibilize immiscible TPS-PE blends by lowering interfacial tension.
engineering_relevance: These validated CG clay models enable faster, larger-scale simulation-driven design of polymer-clay nanocomposites with tunable morphology and improved blend compatibility.
method: Derived initial clay-group interactions from hydration free energies using Lifshitz theory and experimental surface tension data.
Fine-tuned parameters against all-atom TPS-clay structure, thermodynamics, and dynamics.
Applied the CG model to C12TAB-modified MMT in TPS-PE blends to predict interphase compatibilization and morphology.
evidence_signal: The model reproduced structural and dynamic observables from all-atom simulations and estimated TPS component radial distribution and excess entropy accurately, while predicting TPS-PE interfacial tension reduction from 45 mN/m to 13.06 mN/m.
watch_item: Transferability is promising but still depends on how well the clay surface chemistry, organic modifiers, and polymer chemistry match the calibration/validation cases.
paper_title: Characterization and Quantification of Immiscible Polymer Blend Compatibilization by Phyllosilicate Clays
